mechanism: Pair the upper and lower halves of the EXISTING single punched-hole contour with two differently staggered numbered-cell pairs: red14/16 in row3, blue21/23 in row4. Predict B by incorrectly treating two source contour halves as independently shifted layer correspondences. B is invariant under a half-turn but fails the two separate mirror maps; the design targets that orientation/layer substitution. All physical cells and the one hole retain their exact positions.
primary_math_proof: Use original coordinates x,y in [0,6], with row r from top having y in (6-r,7-r). First top-to-bottom fold is y -> 6-y; the stationary stack occupies y in [0,3]. Second left-to-right fold is x -> 6-x; stationary half occupies x in [3,6]. Final packet is translated from this to [16,19]x[0,3]. Its hole is centered (17.5,2.5), so original stationary coordinate is (4.5,2.5). The four preimages are (1.5,2.5),(4.5,2.5),(1.5,3.5),(4.5,3.5), giving rows3/4 and columns2/5, i.e. 14,17,20,23, only C. Exhaustive per-cell folding enumeration is saved. A uses rows2/5 with columns2/5; B,D,E each fail the exact orbit as enumerated. Colored existing grid edges cannot change which cells have a physical hole; even if intrinsic colored ink, the question asks only numbered cells pierced, so C remains uniquely correct.

Four open-L marks restyle existing cell grid edges; all36 numbers remain black and exposed, all fold axes/arrows unchanged. Even literal colored ink on numbered paper does not alter the set of numbered cells physically pierced. The wording asks pierced numbers, not a color-preserving picture. C remains the unique actual orbit.
substantive_difference_from_all_prior_de: Old D candidates paired the full punch outline to one adjacent COLUMN cell (originalcell15 or intermediatecolumn4). Current A design compared whole ROW bands and predicted a uniform rows2/5 offset. New B design has two real punch-contour source parts, four explicit numbered receivers and a layer-dependent COLUMN stagger in rows3/4. It preserves only half-turn pairing in the false receiver set, rather than a wrong rectangular mirror orbit. The new B preset comes from these predeclared cells, not the earlier E output.
